question_text: [Core JavaScript/TypeScript & Browser Runtime - Q41] In the standard browser event loop, in what order are execution queues processed after the current call stack empties?

options.text: All pending microtasks (Promise reactions, queueMicrotask) are drained completely before the next macrotask (setTimeout, setInterval, I/O) is dequeued
One microtask executes, followed by one macrotask in alternating round-robin order
Macrotasks have strict priority over microtasks
Rendering updates occur between every individual microtask

answer_explanation: The microtask queue drains completely until empty before the event loop advances to the next task or performs animation frame rendering callbacks.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: A. Rationale: The microtask queue drains completely until empty before the event loop advances to the next task or performs animation frame rendering callbacks.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Selects the exact correct technical option.
